To celebrate its 10th anniversary, MAAT presents VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos, an exhibition conceived as a dialogue between art and haute couture, inspired by the universe of fashion designer Valentino Garavani (1932–2026).","relevance":"high","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[‘VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos‘ at MAAT this October > The exhibition will be on view at the MAAT Gallery from 2 October 2026 until 22 February 2027.]

To celebrate its 10th anniversary, MAAT presents *VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos*, an exhibition conceived as a dialogue between art and haute couture, inspired by the universe of fashion designer Valentino Garavani (1932–2026).

…

Produced in 2025, ***Valkyrie Venus*** stands at the heart of the exhibition from which it takes its name: an imposing textile sculpture conceived by the artist as a profound reflection on Valentino’s legacy.

Among the new works are ***Crochet Paintings***, a framed series that transforms textiles into a pictorial surface, inspired by a Josef Hoffmann motif featured in the Valentino Garavani Haute Couture Autumn/Winter 1989–90 collection; and ***Sacro Cuore***, a suspended textile sculpture.

The exhibition also includes some of Joana Vasconcelos’s most celebrated works, including ***Marilyn***, the monumental high-heeled shoes made from pots and pan lids; ***Garden of Eden***, an immersive installation inviting visitors to walk through a labyrinth of artificial flowers; and ***Independent Heart #3***, a sculpture made from plastic cutlery that recreates the traditional Heart of Viana.

Presented as part of MAAT’s 10th anniversary programme, this exhibition marks Joana Vasconcelos’ return to the museum and celebrates her longstanding relationship with MAAT and the EDP Foundation. Bringing her artistic practice into dialogue with Valentino, VENUS highlights their shared celebration and commitment to bespoke craftsmanship."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://maat.pt/en/event/exhibiting-publishing-maat-print-2016-2026","title":"Exhibiting, Publishing: MAAT in Print (2016–2026) | MAAT","description":"On the occasion of the museum’s 10th anniversary, Exhibiting, Publishing: MAAT in Print (2016-2026) seeks to take stock of this institutional dimension by acclaiming it, giving it greater visibility and presenting the publications as cultural, artistic and design exhibits which nurture and preserve contemporary thought on art, architecture and technology.","relevance":"high","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Exhibiting, Publishing: MAAT in Print (2016–2026) | MAAT]

MAAT – Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology has established itself over its first decade as an institution particularly dedicated to organising temporary exhibitions, an activity it has pursued alongside the study and public presentation of the EDP Foundation’s collections of contemporary art and energy heritage.

At the same time, the museum established itself as a place for reflection and knowledge production through its publications: exhibition catalogues and guides, monographs and artists’ books, and anthologies of essays. These publications, developed in dialogue with artists, curators, graphic designers, photographers, translators, and other contributors, in step with exhibitions and public programmes, comprise an editorial collection that documents, interprets, and expands the museological experience.

On the occasion of the museum’s 10th anniversary, Exhibiting, Publishing: MAAT in Print (2016-2026) seeks to take stock of this institutional dimension by acclaiming it, giving it greater visibility and presenting the publications as cultural, artistic and design exhibits which nurture and preserve contemporary thought on art, architecture and technology.

…

Created by the Italian foundation, the project was first presented in January 2026 at the cultural space in Rome established by Valentino Garavani and Giancarlo Giammetti, where it remains on display until 19 July 2026. Building on this original concept, the exhibition at MAAT unfolds within a new architectural setting, marking the beginning of a new chapter for the project.

Especially for the occasion, Anna Maria Maiolino will create a dozen of these clay sculptures modelled *in situ*, the largest she has ever produced, with which she will populate the vast space of the room, defining the paths of the public and leading them to establish a strong sensory and poetic relationship with the materiality (in permanent transformation) of the pieces.

results.title: ‘VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos‘ at MAAT this October | MAAT
results.description: The exhibition will be on view at the MAAT Gallery from 2 October 2026 until 22 February 2027. To celebrate its 10th anniversary, MAAT presents VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos, an exhibition conceived as a dialogue between art and haute couture, inspired by the universe of fashion designer Valentino Garavani (1932–2026).

highlights:
[‘VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos‘ at MAAT this October > The exhibition will be on view at the MAAT Gallery from 2 October 2026 until 22 February 2027.]

To celebrate its 10th anniversary, MAAT presents *VENUS – Valentino Garavani Through the Eyes of Joana Vasconcelos*, an exhibition conceived as a dialogue between art and haute couture, inspired by the universe of fashion designer Valentino Garavani (1932–2026).

…

Produced in 2025, ***Valkyrie Venus*** stands at the heart of the exhibition from which it takes its name: an imposing textile sculpture conceived by the artist as a profound reflection on Valentino’s legacy.

Among the new works are ***Crochet Paintings***, a framed series that transforms textiles into a pictorial surface, inspired by a Josef Hoffmann motif featured in the Valentino Garavani Haute Couture Autumn/Winter 1989–90 collection; and ***Sacro Cuore***, a suspended textile sculpture.

The exhibition also includes some of Joana Vasconcelos’s most celebrated works, including ***Marilyn***, the monumental high-heeled shoes made from pots and pan lids; ***Garden of Eden***, an immersive installation inviting visitors to walk through a labyrinth of artificial flowers; and ***Independent Heart #3***, a sculpture made from plastic cutlery that recreates the traditional Heart of Viana.

Presented as part of MAAT’s 10th anniversary programme, this exhibition marks Joana Vasconcelos’ return to the museum and celebrates her longstanding relationship with MAAT and the EDP Foundation. Bringing her artistic practice into dialogue with Valentino, VENUS highlights their shared celebration and commitment to bespoke craftsmanship.

highlights:
[Exhibiting, Publishing: MAAT in Print (2016–2026) | MAAT]

MAAT – Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology has established itself over its first decade as an institution particularly dedicated to organising temporary exhibitions, an activity it has pursued alongside the study and public presentation of the EDP Foundation’s collections of contemporary art and energy heritage.

At the same time, the museum established itself as a place for reflection and knowledge production through its publications: exhibition catalogues and guides, monographs and artists’ books, and anthologies of essays. These publications, developed in dialogue with artists, curators, graphic designers, photographers, translators, and other contributors, in step with exhibitions and public programmes, comprise an editorial collection that documents, interprets, and expands the museological experience.

On the occasion of the museum’s 10th anniversary, Exhibiting, Publishing: MAAT in Print (2016-2026) seeks to take stock of this institutional dimension by acclaiming it, giving it greater visibility and presenting the publications as cultural, artistic and design exhibits which nurture and preserve contemporary thought on art, architecture and technology.

highlights:
[Tours to the exhibition Anna Maria Maiolino – Poetic Earth | MAAT]

25/03/2026 - 31/08/2026

…

Anna Maria Maiolino – Poetic Earth, at MAAT's Oval Gallery, presents a selection of drawings and photos from the 1970s and 1980s, which shed light on the early stages of her work, while also establishing a productive relationship with the clay sculptures she began working on in the 1980s, which are the focus of this exhibition. Especially for the occasion, Anna Maria Maiolino will create a dozen of these clay sculptures modelled *in situ*, the largest she has ever produced, with which she will populate the vast space of the room, defining the paths of the public and leading them to establish a strong sensory and poetic relationship with the materiality (in permanent transformation) of the pieces.
